mutant:features/duplicates.feature#A fol.reason: All eight are invariance by design, which is the scenario purpose. SUPPLEMENTAL and REOPENED both resolve NOT_EVALUATED with reason FOLLOW_ON_NOTICE_TYPE, so swapping them cannot change the outcome. The near date (2026-06-02) and far date (2026-12-01) resolve identically because the window comparison never runs for these types - which is what the far rows exist to prove, and they are NOT redundant with the near rows: an implementation that consulted the window before the notice type would return no-match rather than NOT_EVALUATED on the far rows, and only they catch it. Do not prune these rows as duplicative. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if SUPPLEMENTAL and REOPENED ever resolve differently from one another, or if any notice type exclusion becomes conditional on timing.

mutant:features/duplicates.feature#Match.reason: Three mechanisms across ten mutants, recorded under one reason because approval is scoped per scenario and not per mutant - and because approve stamps every survivor in the scenario, not only the ones the gate reports as unapproved. Read this as three records. (a) Rows already excluded on a single dimension - the policy-mismatch row and the loss-type-mismatch row - yield no match whatever the mutated column holds, so mutating any other dimension on them is inert. Four mutants. (b) Rows excluded by loss-date distance: their policy number and their loss type both agree with the existing claim, so neither is what excludes them, and substituting either leaves the outcome unchanged. Four mutants. (c) Matching rows whose loss date is swapped for another in-window date: the substituted date is also inside the window, so the match survives - a swap to an out-of-window date flips the result and is killed, which means the boundary is proven by the in-window and out-of-window rows jointly and never by a single row. Two mutants. Rows are described by role rather than by literal value, per the convention in docs/harness-findings.md: example data is what a vocabulary pass changes, so a reason quoting it decays while its locator stays valid. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if the window changes from 60 days, if policy or loss-type equality stops being part of the match key, or if this Examples table gains a second row whose policy number matches the existing claim.

mutant:features/siu_indicators.feature#A.reason: Guard-dominated. The mutated value is the UPPER bound, but this scenario exercises the LOWER bound: the inception date postdates the loss date, so the `0 <=` check in _is_recent_inception rejects the negative interval before the upper bound is consulted. The upper bound is unreachable here at any value. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if the `0 <=` lower bound is removed, relaxed, or replaced.

mutant:features/siu_indicators.feature#B.reason: Margin, not inertness. The threshold is doing its job; the example values sit far enough from it that a plus-or-minus-one mutation cannot cross the boundary - 62 days against 45/46, and 40 days against both 45/46 and 30/31. The boundaries themselves are proven in the dedicated boundary scenarios, which are where a one-day mutation does kill. REVISIT TRIGGER: void if either scenario's example dates are changed such that an interval lands within one day of its threshold.

mutant:features/siu_indicators.feature#N.reason: The threshold is deliberately inert in this scenario. No policy inception date is present, so recent policy inception resolves to NOT_EVALUATED with reason NO_POLICY_INCEPTION_DATE regardless of the threshold's value. The threshold is supplied precisely to prove the NOT_EVALUATED result comes from the missing input rather than a missing threshold - isolating that variable is the scenario's purpose, so a mutation to it correctly changes nothing.

mutant:features/triage.feature#From raw.reason:
All eleven survivors in this scenario are equivalent, for two distinct reasons.
They share one record because `gauntlet mutant approve` applies a single reason
to every survivor in scope and all eleven fall in this scenario.

TEN OF ELEVEN are ordinary equivalents: the mutated value produces identical
severity, queue, and both SIU indicators. Loss-amount mutations (400.00->401.00,
50000->50001) cannot change any expected value, because severity derives from
loss type alone and nothing in the domain reads the amount. That independence is
what the loss_amount column is deliberately retained to demonstrate (ASSUMPTIONS.md,
item 4c). This supersedes the previous justification for the theft rows, which
cited a $500 threshold: that rule was deleted in item 4c, and the theft rows now
survive for exactly the same reason as fire and water_damage. Inception mutations
to 2026-05-15 against a 2026-08-01 loss date are 78 days out, outside the 30-day
window either way.

THE ELEVENTH — theft / 2026-06-15, inception_date 2024-01-01->2026-07-20 — is a
separate judgment and this paragraph is its own record. The mutated inception date
postdates that row's loss date, producing a negative interval that resolves FALSE
only because of the `0 <=` lower bound in _is_recent_inception. That guard IS
documented, contrary to this approval's previous text: siu_indicators.feature's
scenario "An inception date later than the loss date does not fire the indicator"
specifies it, and tests/unit/test_siu.py exercises it. The mutant is unkillable at
this layer not because the specification is silent, but because this scenario
asserts routing invariance rather than indicator boundaries — the behaviour is
specified, just not here. It is structurally unavoidable rather than a data-choice
artifact: this scenario must exercise recent_inception=TRUE (an inception within
30 days of that row's loss date) and late_reporting=TRUE (a loss date more than 45
days before today), which together guarantee that some inception value in the
column postdates some loss date in the column.

REVISIT TRIGGER, applying only to the eleventh mutant and not the other ten: this
approval is void if the `0 <=` lower bound in _is_recent_inception is removed,
relaxed, or replaced. Removal would now also fail siu_indicators.feature and
test_siu.py. The previous text's claim that nothing else in the suite would catch
it was true when first recorded on 2026-08-09 and false by the time it was
re-stamped on 2026-08-10; it is corrected here.
